slot.brief: Standard YDSE with given slit separation and screen distance; compute fringe width, or number of fringes in a given screen length.

stem: In a Young’s double-slit experiment, light of wavelength $500$ nm is used with slit separation $0.20$ mm and a screen distance of $1.2$ m. How many fringe spacings fit in a screen segment of length $18$ mm?

verdicts.working: Fringe spacing: β = λD/d = (500×10⁻⁹)(1.2)/(0.20×10⁻³) = 3 mm. Thus 18 mm contains 18/3 = 6 spacings.

working:
$\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}=\dfrac{(500\times10^{-9})(1.2)}{0.20\times10^{-3}}=3$ mm
$N=\dfrac{18}{3}=6$

Independent check: Fringe spacing: β = λD/d = (500×10⁻⁹)(1.2)/(0.20×10⁻³) = 3 mm. Thus 18 mm contains 18/3 = 6 spacings.
solution:
Fringe spacing is $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}=\dfrac{(500\times10^{-9})(1.2)}{0.20\times10^{-3}}=3\text{ mm}.$
Number of spacings in $18$ mm: $N=\dfrac{18}{3}=6$.
